newsitem.title: USA: UAW hits GM parts plants with two strike deadlines.
newsitem.headline: UAW hits GM parts plants with two strike deadlines.

text.p: The United Auto Workers, threatening General Motors Corp. again with paralysing parts shortages, said on Tuesday it issued new strike deadlines at two GM components plants in Michigan and Indiana.

The UAW said its members may walk off the job at midnight July 22 at a transmission plant in Warren, Mich., and a Delphi Interior & Lighting Systems plant in Anderson, Ind., if no new contract is reached.

The two plants are critical facilities for GM. The Warren plant supplies four-speed automatic transmissions for front wheel drive cars and light trucks, including GM's new minivans. Workers at UAW Local 663 in Anderson make tail lamps for nearly all of GM's vehicles.
Al Benchich, president of Local 909 in Warren, said contract talks have stalled around staffing and outsourcing, the practice of farming out work to outside suppliers.
"The issues are basically the same issues throughout all of General Motors," he said. "Not enough people and outsourcing of jobs."
Talks are continuing to settle a nearly three-month old UAW strike at GM's full-size pickup truck plant in Pontiac, Mich.
